findings.title: Server hybrid search issues a request for every keystroke
findings.what: The effect invokes fetchSearch immediately whenever query changes. Typing a query therefore starts one server hybrid-search request per keystroke. Aborting the previous browser request does not guarantee that already-started server-side lexical/semantic work is cancelled, so normal typing can multiply request and compute load.
findings.fix: Debounce the effective server query by a short interval before constructing the request, while retaining AbortController cancellation for requests that have already started.
findings.acceptance: Add a fake-timer interaction test that enters several characters within the debounce interval, advances the timer, and verifies fetchSearch is called exactly once with the final query; also verify a subsequent settled query triggers one additional call.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarially re-read src/components/SearchView.tsx:99-153 and src/components/SearchView.test.ts:215-255 at the pinned baseline. The local fallback is intentional, but the server effect has no timer or deferred query and depends directly on every query value; the existing server-search test covers only a single change and supplies no request-rate guard.
